decisions.text: Teletext function will be dropped from the new remote control.
Audio settings (mono, stereo, pitch, bass) and screen settings (brightness, colour) will be included despite being less used.
The new remote will include an LCD screen and speech recognition features.
The remote design must retain the corporate logo and colours.
The remote control will target users under forty, specifically focusing on the age range of sixteen to forty.
Basic functions will be on the remote, while advanced options will be hidden in an on-screen menu.
The power button will be placed on the top right of the remote.
The screen will be placed at the bottom of the remote.
The display and microphone are placed on top of the remote control.
The corporate logo is placed on the top left of the remote.
The remote includes sound settings for treble, bass, pitch, and mono/stereo.
The remote includes image settings for brightness and contrast.

notes:
## Target Audience and Functional Requirements
- Research showed current remotes are ugly and bad for RSI; the new product targets users under forty (specifically sixteen to forty).
- Teletext is considered outdated and will be dropped. Classic functions like power, channel, and volume must be kept.
- Users under forty are interested in an LCD screen and speech recognition, which will be included.
- Audio settings (mono, stereo, pitch, bass) and screen settings (brightness, colour) will be included despite being less used.
## Design Layout and Features
- The remote design must retain the corporate logo and colours and look like part of the room's interior.
- The display and microphone are placed on top of the remote control for better usability.
- The corporate logo is placed on the top left of the remote.
- The remote includes sound settings for treble, bass, pitch, and mono/stereo, and image settings for brightness and contrast.
- The remote includes channel programming with autoseek and swap channel functionality.
- The remote control layout will be separated into basic functions and advanced functions with a visual line.
- The remote control will feature a menu button, an OK button, a back button, and multifunctional navigation arrows.
- LED lights under the buttons will be used to indicate which buttons are active for the current function.
tldr: The team designed a new remote control targeting users under forty, featuring an LCD screen and speech recognition. They decided to drop teletext but keep audio and image settings, hiding advanced options in a menu. The layout includes the screen and microphone on top, basic buttons on the right, and LED indicators.
